{{nihongo|'''Iwatsuhime Shrine'''|伊和都比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

'''Iwatsuhime Shrine''' (いわつひめじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Cape Misaki|Q11488946|qid=Q11488946}}, {{ill|Akō, Hyōgo|Q424813|qid=Q424813}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

Located in the {{ill|Akō-Misaki Onsen|Q11635887|qid=Q11635887}} area, it stands facing the sea. It is worshiped for sailing safety and matchmaking<ref name="kobe-np20220807">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.kobe-np.co.jp/news/sougou/202208/0015535551.shtml |title=Panoramic Seto Inland Sea glamping: luxury dome tents, sauna, and BBQ with local oysters opens in Ako on the 11th |accessdate=2022-08-08|date=2022-08-07|publisher=Kobe Shimbun}}</ref>.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity is Iwatsuhime Ōkami. Originally this may have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyouke-hime}}, or the {{ill|Himegami|Q22070227|qid=Q22070227|lt=female deity}} of Ōanamuchi-no-Kami, deity of Iwaza Ōanamochi Mitama Shrine (present {{ill|Iwa Shrine (Matsumoto)|Q65320|qid=Q65320}}), ichinomiya of {{ill|Harima Province|be|Харыма (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Harima|ceb|Harima (baranggay sa Hapon)|cs|Provincie Harima|de|Provinz Harima|es|Provincia de Harima|fa|ولایت هاریما|fr|Province de Harima|gl|Provincia de Harima|id|Provinsi Harima|it|Harima (provincia)|ja|播磨国|ko|하리마국|lt|Harimos žemė|nl|Harima (provincie)|pt|Província de Harima|ru|Харима (провинция)|simple|Harima Province|sk|Harima (provincia)|sr|Провинција Харима|tr|Harima (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Харіма|zh|播磨國|zh_min_nan|Harima-kok|qid=Q1047523}}. It has long been called "Misaki Myōjin."

=== History ===
An ancient shrine listed first among three shrines of {{ill|Akō District, Hyōgo|Q1042141|qid=Q1042141}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}.

A shrine formerly on the offshore reef "Hatchō-iwa" was moved to the current site in {{ill|Tenna|Q1145289|qid=Q1145289|lt=Tenna}} 3 ({{ill|1683|Q7651|qid=Q7651}}) of the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} by {{ill|Asano Naganao|Q2866309|qid=Q2866309}}. In the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, {{ill|Tōgō Heihachirō|Q296785|qid=Q296785}} visited here before the outbreak of the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|Q159950|qid=Q159950}} to pray for victory<ref name="kobe-np20220807" />. Because of this, it gained devotion from {{ill|Imperial Japanese Navy|Q219712|qid=Q219712|lt=Imperial Navy}} personnel, and until before the war, Combined Fleet commanders including Togo worshiped from ships at sea<ref name="kobe-np20220807" />. Even today, sailors actively worship from the sea for navigation safety and big catches.

=== Iwatsuhime Shrine of Akashi District ===
In the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, an Iwatsuhime Shrine of {{ill|Akashi District, Hyōgo|Q11512561|qid=Q11512561}} in Harima Province is also listed. Today there is no same-name shrine in former Akashi District; candidate shrines are {{ill|Inazume Shrine|Q11596731|qid=Q11596731}} in Ōkura Honmachi, Akashi, Inazumehama Ebisu Shrine (a sessha within Inazume Shrine), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Izanami Shrine}} in Misaki-chō, Akashi, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwaya Shrine}} in Zaimoku-chō, Akashi.
